title: fix-network use cases
description: What a developer does with fix-network in a terminal, step by step: find out what is wrong, then repair it.

entities.name: Find out what is wrong with the Mac's network
entities.description: A developer whose internet, VPN or intranet is not working runs a read-only diagnosis.
entities.goal: Learn which layer of the network is broken and what it takes to fix each problem, without changing anything.
preconditions: The developer is at a terminal on a Mac with fix-network installed.
For corporate DNS and services to be checked, the developer knows an internal host (and port) to name with --internal-host.
postconditions: The checks, findings and outcomes are on the screen (or as JSON) and in diagnostic.log, and the settings found are in original.json.
The exit status is 0 when no dimension failed, else 1.

flow.action: Runs fix-network diagnose, naming internal hosts with --internal-host and adding -v or --json if wanted.
Creates the run's state directory, takes a snapshot of the network and saves the original settings.
Judges the seven dimensions and records each problem as a finding with its remedy.
Prints the checks, each finding with its outcome and the fix command line for the fixable ones, what was not verified, and whether a Wi-Fi reset is required.
Reads the outcomes: runs the suggested fix command, does what a manual remedy says, or reboots.

alternatives.condition: The machine is not a Mac.
alternatives.outcome: The tool says it works on macOS only and exits with status 2 before touching the machine.

alternatives.condition: The state directory cannot be created.
alternatives.outcome: The tool says so on stderr and exits with status 1.
Corporate DNS and corporate service are NOT TESTED, and the report asks for --internal-host HOST:PORT.
Only the JSON document is printed on stdout.

entities.name: Repair the Mac's network
entities.description: A developer lets fix-network repair what the diagnosis found, allowing the steps the evidence calls for.
entities.goal: Get the network working again with as little disruption as possible, and see that it does.
preconditions: The developer is at a terminal on a Mac with fix-network installed.
For privileged steps, the developer can use sudo.
postconditions: Every step that ran is listed as ok or FAILED with its reason.
Every dimension, internal hosts included, has been checked again after the repair.
The exit status is 0 when no dimension failed, else 1.

flow.action: Runs fix-network fix with the same --internal-host as the diagnosis, adding --vpn, --fix-proxy, --allow-route-flush, --allow-remote or --force as wanted.
Creates the run's state directory, takes a snapshot and saves the original settings.
Assesses the snapshot and runs the least disruptive allowed step not yet tried, checking every command's exit status.
Types their password when sudo asks for it in the terminal.
Takes a fresh snapshot and assesses again; repeats the step and recheck until healthy or nothing more is allowed.
Waits 15 seconds, gathers everything again and prints the final report and the actions.

alternatives.outcome: The diagnosis and the plan are printed, with the flag each blocked step needs, and nothing is changed.

alternatives.condition: Every remaining step needs a flag that was not given, or every remedy is manual or a reboot.
alternatives.outcome: No step runs; the report says 'fixable but not allowed' with the flags to add, or gives the manual or reboot advice.

alternatives.condition: The tool runs inside an SSH session without --allow-remote.
alternatives.outcome: Steps that can cut the session are skipped and reported as needing --allow-remote.

alternatives.condition: There is no terminal for sudo to ask in.
alternatives.outcome: sudo -n fails and the step is recorded as FAILED.

alternatives.condition: A step failed or did not help, and the finding has no untried step left.
alternatives.outcome: The finding falls back to its manual or reboot advice, for example signing in to the VPN from the menu bar.
The tool does not wait; it reports the first snapshot.

relatedViews.relationship: The commands these use cases call.
The same goals pursued by a coding agent on the developer's behalf.
